articles.body: Patching Is Not Provisioning: What the October 2026 KEV Wave Says About Edge Device Lifecycle Between late September and mid-October 2026, CISA added a series of vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog in rapid succession. Citrix NetScaler, F5 BIG-IP, Cisco Secure Email Gateway, Ivanti Connect Secure, Palo Alto PAN-OS, Atlassian Data Center, BeyondTrust Remote Support, AhsayCBS. Different vendors, different flaw classes, one shared property: every one of them is infrastructure that sits at a trust boundary. That clustering is not coincidence, and treating each incident separately misses the operational lesson.

Fixing it became the first real test of whether “self-hosted, one click” actually holds up for something we’d use ourselves, not just something we built for other people’s apps. What we launched# Plausible Community Edition, as a Railyard stack template: three services — Plausible itself, Postgres for its own app data, and ClickHouse for the actual analytics events — provisioned together on one of our own servers. railyard launch plausible --server Copy That’s the whole provisioning step.

articles.title: Which AI bots visit my website? I counted for 30 days
articles.excerpt: First published on yappatyih.com. AI crawler detection means finding out which bots that collect pages for AI companies visit your website, how often, and what they read, usually from the name each bo…
articles.body: First published on yappatyih.com . TL;DR AI crawler detection means finding out which bots that collect pages for AI companies visit your website, how often, and what they read, usually from the name each bot gives in its requests. In the 30 days to 20 October 2026, Cloudflare counted about 4,040 requests to this site from the AI crawlers it recognises. Google sent the most, then Anthropic, OpenAI, Apple and Microsoft. About half of the successful requests were for training AI models. Only 26 were an AI assistant fetching a page because a person asked it something. The crawlers read my sitemaps more than any post, some "AI crawlers" were scanners hunting for password files, and all that reading did not get me cited: ChatGPT named this site in 0 of 12 answers on 17 October.

articles.title: Investigating the Return of the PHP2Shell Nightmare
articles.excerpt: The public PoC claiming “RCE via a PHP core UAF” did not work in my lab. After reading the official patches, the actual causes turned out to be state corruption during OOM handling and state left behi…
articles.body: The public PoC claiming “RCE via a PHP core UAF” did not work in my lab. After reading the official patches, the actual causes turned out to be state corruption during OOM handling and state left behind across requests—not a zval UAF within a single request. What this article concludes I built a local Docker lab to investigate the PHP vulnerability making headlines as “php2shell,” compared the public PoC with PHP source code, and then read the patch diffs published with the official releases. The result: the “PHP core UAF” described by the public PoC did not reproduce, and the official root causes were different. However, a chain combining the session.upload_progress write primitive with an application-level LFI did work.

articles.title: BioWare Was the Greatest RPG Developer Ever
articles.excerpt: There are many great role-playing game developers, past and present. But none can touch what BioWare has done over 30-plus years.
articles.body: BioWare is dead , and my feelings are a strange cocktail of anger, sadness, and Jack’s Complete Lack of Surprise. The legendary RPG studio was bought by a private investment group earlier this year, and history shows that venture capital frequently kills what it touches, extracting whatever value out of it that it can before moving onto the next victim. It’s a hell of a contrast to the beginning of BioWare, which started out as such a pure thing. Two practicing doctors, Ray Muzyka and Greg Zeschuk, quit medicine to pursue their dream of making computer role-playing games. Sure, the studio was bought and sold a couple of times between then and now, and yes, BioWare’s recent results haven’t lived up to its venerable past, but my goodness, what a legacy this studio leaves behind.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor. Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. (Launch occurred at 8:52 p.m. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. 22.) It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov. 14. The rest of the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft stayed in orbit, where it collected and transmitted data from the moon to Earth for about a year.

articles.title: Sci-fi legend Alan Dean Foster on his new futuristic adventure 'Lost On Paradise': 'It's paradise until you get there, and then maybe you mess it up' (interview)
articles.excerpt: 'Maybe Paradise isn’t always Paradise.'
articles.body: Few names in the science fiction literary world carry as much weight and respect as author Alan Dean Foster. His award-winning 55-year career as a grandmaster of the genre continues with his latest novel from Blackstone Publishing, " Lost on Paradise ", and we have an exclusive excerpt to share with our readers ahead of its release this week. Foster famously ghost-wrote the first " Star Wars " novelization for George Lucas in 1976 and "Splinter of the Mind’s Eye" in 1978, which was intended to be a low-budget Star Wars sequel should the space opera not become a hit. He’s been a mainstay for go-to fantastic adventures featuring engaging characters, dynamic plotlines, and imaginative worlds for six decades.
